source.title: A Two-Phase Perspective on Deep Learning Dynamics
source.citation: R. de Mello Koch et al., 2025
source.authors: R. de Mello Koch; Animik Ghosh

record.tranche_reason: The study measures test error over training time and reports double-descent curves in new model and dataset settings.
record.gate_note: The study's own test-error plots over training steps are rows. The discussion of model-size and sample-size double descent, and cited results about grokking and circuit complexity, are not additional results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study plots its own test-error curves over training steps for a 2-layer transformer on algorithmic grokking tasks. It reports epoch-wise double descent in a new setting with no label noise and weight decay 0. The model, data, measure and protocol differ from the original, so this is T3 rather than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also argue that I(T;X) serves as a progress measure. They argue that the compression phase is not actively optimized by standard training and may be unnecessarily prolonged. They draw a renormalization-group analogy in which the second phase is principled forgetting.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures test error over training steps in a two-layer transformer on algorithmic datasets; it does not report reproducing the original study's full protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The dataset changes the reported timing: the fitting/generalization transition is around 5 × 10^3 steps for division modulo 96 and around 10^5 steps for S5; the S5 compression phase is described as longer.

fits_no_version.finding: The onset of the second descent in test error over training steps coincides with training error reaching zero, with grokking onset, and with the start of information-bottleneck compression (the rightmost point of the information-plane trajectory). This holds on both datasets, at about 5×10^3 steps for mod 96 and about 10^5 steps for S5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In epoch-wise double descent, the second descent begins when training error reaches zero and coincides with the onset of representation compression (falling I(T;X)) and with grokking.

record.problems: The evidence covers one stated architecture and two algorithmic datasets. Test-error values are presented in plots without exact numerical values or reported uncertainty, and no controls are described.
record.rows_left_out: No other own test-error outcomes bearing on the claim are reported. The layer-depth discussion concerns mutual information, not a measure named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Only one architecture and two algorithmic datasets. No label noise, no image benchmarks, no other optimizers. Curves are over steps and likely use loss rather than error.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epoch and sample axes. The study only reports timing alignment on the training-time axis.
No label-noise or regularization sweep, and no test for multiple peaks.
No recounting of complexity via effective parameters.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is qualitative: two figures, single runs, and no uncertainty or controls. The 'Physical Review E' peer-review status in the record is not stated in the text, which is an arXiv v1 preprint. Treat that status as unverified.

versions.untested_parts: The curves use training steps, not epochs; no other architectures or training settings are tested.
No training-sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold is reported.
The study does not test a capacity sweep across model classes.
It compares timing of training-time phenomena, but does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample axes.
No label-noise or regularization sweep, or test for multiple peaks, is reported.
The study does not recount complexity using an effective parameter measure or test whether that changes the curve shape.
